column2: L'arte del violino: 24 Caprices
My left hand reaches heights no one has yet visited.
Skills schooled in Rome, in your orchestra.
A virtuoso trained in Rome. The 24 caprices attached to his concertos foreshadowed Paganini.
Jumping from the window was a small misunderstanding, you see.
There are not two virtuosos like me in Europe.
A genius known for his arrogance. In 1722, after a dispute with a colleague in Dresden, he leapt from a window and hurt his leg. Afterwards he found refuge in Prague.
Vivaldi: violin concerto
I have always played behind the grille of the Pietà.
Just once, I should like to play outside the grille.
An orphan raised at the Ospedale della Pietà in Venice who became a virtuoso. Vivaldi wrote many concertos for her.
I am studying with Herr Pisendel.
One day, concertmaster of your orchestra.
A young man who studied with Pisendel in Dresden. He would later be concertmaster of the orchestra of Crown Prince Frederick of Prussia.
24 Matinées
The Concert Spirituel is as good as my own garden.
The French violin, for your orchestra.
A virtuoso whom Viotti called 'the French Tartini'. He later became the first professor of violin at the Paris Conservatoire.
42 Études
Études? I can write as many as you like.
The bow of young Paris, for your orchestra.
A young violinist of Paris. Beethoven later dedicated a sonata to him, which he is said never once to have played.
Adagio? In my country nobody plays slowly.
If you can promise me pay to match Her Majesty the Empress's.
An eccentric virtuoso at the court of Catherine II. Peerless in fast passages, he is said to have been poor in slow music.
Mozart: Violin Sonata, K. 454
Herr Mozart's music always arrives at the last minute.
In your orchestra I shall play as if singing.
A celebrated woman violinist. In 1784 Mozart wrote the Sonata K. 454 for her and played the concert with his own part still a blank page.
I lead the orchestras of London.
Leadership schooled in London, for your orchestra.
Born in Mannheim, a great leader of London orchestras. His improved 'Cramer' bow was ahead of its time.
In Mannheim bowing, unanimity is everything.
I shall bring the strings of your orchestra together.
A violinist of the Mannheim school. He moved to Munich with the court.
Violin Concerto No. 8 'in modo di scena cantante'
Paganini's acrobatics lack breeding.
The true German violin, for your orchestra.
Court Kapellmeister in Kassel and Germany's foremost violinist. He invented the chin rest and is counted among the first to use a baton.
Mendelssohn: Violin Concerto
Mendelssohn and I have been friends since childhood.
As concertmaster of your orchestra.
Later concertmaster of the Gewandhaus; he advised on Mendelssohn's concerto and gave its premiere.
Souvenirs de Norvège
The sound of Norway's waterfalls, straight onto the violin.
The bow of the North, for your orchestra.
A self-taught Norwegian virtuoso. He went to Paris in 1831, was fired up by hearing Paganini, and was later called 'the Paganini of the North'.
I have scarcely ever left Vienna.
The sweet tone of Vienna, for your orchestra.
A celebrated violinist of the Viennese court. His brilliant style made him enormously popular in Vienna.
Paganini: Violin Concerto No. 2
I am Maestro Paganini's one and only pupil.
My master's art, for your orchestra.
The only pupil Paganini ever took. His master gave him a fine copy of 'Il Cannone', his own violin, made by Vuillaume.
De Bériot: violin concerto
Monsieur de Bériot often praises me.
I want to play on bigger stages.
A Belgian prodigy. A pupil of de Bériot, he was touring while still in his teens. He would become a great master of the Franco-Belgian school.
Violin Concerto No. 2
After London, my students in Brussels are waiting.
The Polish bow, for your orchestra.
A great Polish violinist. After serving as soloist to the Russian court he became a professor at the Brussels Conservatoire.
Wieniawski: concerto
'A woman, playing the violin!' they used to say.
I shall take the stage with your orchestra.
A woman violinist from Moravia. Hugely popular in London, she later became Lady Hallé.
Bach: 'Air on the G String' (arrangement)
I lead the orchestra at Bayreuth.
The concertmaster of the Festspielhaus, for your orchestra.
Concertmaster at the first Bayreuth Festival in 1876. He arranged Bach's air and made it famous as the 'Air on the G String'.
Tchaikovsky: Violin Concerto
If no one will play Tchaikovsky's concerto, I will.
A new concerto, with your orchestra.
Professor at the Moscow Conservatory. He later gave the premiere of Tchaikovsky's concerto, which had been called 'unplayable'.
Set pieces studied with Joachim
I am learning my craft under Professor Joachim.
A young Hungarian bow, for your orchestra.
A young Hungarian studying with Joachim in Berlin. He will become a celebrated professor in Budapest.
Professor Auer scolded me a good deal.
My tone, in your orchestra.
A boy genius from Auer's class. He made his London debut in 1905 at 14. Known for the sweet sound called the 'Elman tone'.
Glazunov: concerto
Professor Auer's class is hard going — all geniuses.
Let me try my hand in your orchestra.
A young man studying with Auer at the St Petersburg Conservatory. He later became a famous teacher in America.
At 14 I played the concerto before Herr Brahms.
The sound of the Polish soul, for your orchestra.
A Polish-born genius. In 1896, aged 13, he played the concerto before Brahms and is said to have moved the composer to tears.
I am only twelve, but please do not treat me as a child.
My bow, for your orchestra.
A prodigy from Hubay's class. He made his Berlin debut in 1903 at the age of 10 and won acclaim in London the next year. Sibelius dedicated his concerto to him.
Tchaikovsky: Violin Concerto (American premiere)
America has violinists too.
The bow of the New World, for your orchestra.
A leading American violinist. She studied with Joachim and gave the American premieres of the Tchaikovsky and Sibelius concertos.
Sibelius: Violin Concerto (premiere of the revised version)
I am second violin of the Joachim Quartet.
The sure bow of Berlin, for your orchestra.
Born in Bohemia, Joachim's right hand. In 1905 he gave the premiere of the revised Sibelius concerto under R. Strauss.
Paganini: Caprices
I have played all of Paganini in a single evening.
Transcendent technique, for your orchestra.
A German virtuoso. He was to have given the premiere of Sibelius's concerto but missed the chance over scheduling.
I once played on street corners.
In your orchestra, let me dream once more.
An English woman violinist. Born poor, she played in the streets, but her talent was discovered and she reached the first rank.
Beethoven: string quartets
I have been concertmaster of the Vienna Philharmonic for twenty-odd years.
The sound of Vienna, for your orchestra.
Celebrated concertmaster of the Vienna Philharmonic and husband of Mahler's sister. He led the Rosé Quartet.

Viol
Pièces de viole
They say Monsieur Marais plays like an angel, and I like a devil.
The devil's viol, in your orchestra.
A virtuoso of transcendent technique on the viol (viola da gamba). It was said: 'Marais plays like an angel, Forqueray like a devil.'
Lute
Lute suite
They call me the last great master of the lute, and such things.
The lute of the Dresden court, for your orchestra.
The great lutenist of the Dresden court, one of the best-paid musicians of his day. He is said to have matched improvisations with Bach.
Trumpet
The trumpet parts of Bach's cantatas
No one but I can play these high notes.
A trumpet for your orchestra's festivities.
Senior town musician of Leipzig, who played the high trumpet parts in Bach's cantatas. His portrait shows him holding a coiled trumpet.
Cello sonata
In Naples they call me Francischello.
The song of the cello, for your orchestra.
A celebrated cellist of Naples. According to Geminiani, A. Scarlatti said after playing with him that 'only an angel in human form could play like that'.
Cello Concerto in B-flat major
I live quietly at the Spanish court.
The sound of the cello and the string quintet, for your orchestra.
A cello virtuoso and composer. While serving Spanish royalty he published a great many works in Paris. The famous 'Minuet' is a movement of a string quintet.
Haydn: Cello Concerto No. 2
I have played under Kapellmeister Haydn for years now.
The bass of the Esterházys, for your orchestra.
Principal cellist to the Esterházy family. Haydn's Cello Concerto in D was written for him.
Viola
Viola Concerto in D major
The viola, too, knows the joy of the solo.
The voice of the viola, for your orchestra.
Son of the great master of the Mannheim school and a virtuoso of the viola and viola d'amore. His viola concerto is still an audition standard.
Horn
Horn concerto
My real name is Jan Václav Stich. I am a fugitive, you see.
The miracle of the horn, for your orchestra.
A great horn virtuoso from Bohemia. He ran away from the count he served and changed his name. Beethoven later wrote a horn sonata for him.
Mozart: horn concertos
Young Mozart writes rude remarks about me in the score.
